title: Cohomology along an affine morphism: the edge map is an isomorphism
statement: Let $h:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism] (for instance a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]) and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $R^ph_*\mathcal F=0$ for $p>0$ [pqf-def-cohomology], and for every $p\ge0$ the edge map $e_{h,\mathcal F}:H^p(S,h_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (c) (the map induced by the $h$-map $\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$) is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S(S)$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology, line 202) and its proof: Lemma 01XC (lemma-relative-affine-vanishing, line 181) and the Leray spectral sequence, Cohomology, Lemma 01F4 (cohomology-lemma-apply-Leray) part (1), whose identification is the edge map of Equation 01FA; used in Lemma 02OD's proof ('By the Leray spectral sequence for i_n')

proof.text: (Vanishing of the higher direct images.) Since $h$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] (a closed immersion is affine, by the same definition node) and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, $R^ph_*\mathcal F=0$ for all $p>0$ by [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] (Stacks 01XC: $R^ph_*\mathcal F$ is the sheaf associated to $V\mapsto H^p(h^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$, and for $V$ affine $h^{-1}(V)$ is affine, where quasi-coherent cohomology vanishes). This is the first assertion.

(The direct image of an injective resolution is a $\Gamma$-acyclic resolution.) Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules ($\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$). By the definition of cohomology and of higher direct images [pqf-def-cohomology], $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $R^ph_*\mathcal F=H^p(h_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$, with $R^0h_*\mathcal F=h_*\mathcal F$ because $h_*$ is left exact, so $\alpha:h_*\mathcal F\to h_*\mathcal I^0$ identifies $h_*\mathcal F$ with $\ker(h_*\mathcal I^0\to h_*\mathcal I^1)$. Together with step 1 the augmented complex $0\to h_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\alpha}h_*\mathcal I^0\to h_*\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ is exact, i.e. $\alpha:h_*\mathcal F\to h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ ($h_*\mathcal F$ placed in degree $0$) is a quasi-isomorphism which is a monomorphism in every degree. Each $h_*\mathcal I^q$ is acyclic for $\Gamma(S,-)$ on $\mathcal O_S$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injective-acyclic]. So $h_*\mathcal F\to h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution of $h_*\mathcal F$ by $\Gamma(S,-)$-acyclic objects.

source.place: Remark 01F0 (remark-elucidate-lemma, line 2147): Rf_*F is represented by f_*I^•, and Gamma(Y, f_*I^•) computes RGamma(Y, Rf_*F) by Lemma 01EX (lemma-pushforward-injective) and Leray's acyclicity lemma

proof.text: (The acyclic resolution computes $H^p(S,h_*\mathcal F)$.) Choose an injective resolution $s:h_*\mathcal F\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_S$-modules with $\mathcal J^q=0$ for $q<0$. Since $\alpha$ of step 2 is a quasi-isomorphism of bounded below complexes which is a monomorphism in each degree and $\mathcal J^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, there is a morphism of complexes $\gamma:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ with $\gamma\circ\alpha=s$ [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso]; $\gamma$ is a quasi-isomorphism because $\alpha$ and $s$ are. By Leray's acyclicity lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (2), applied to the left exact functor $\Gamma(S,-)$ on $\mathcal O_S$-modules (an abelian category with enough injectives, [pqf-def-cohomology]), to the resolution $h_*\mathcal F\to h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ by $\Gamma(S,-)$-acyclic objects of step 2 and to the morphism $\gamma$ over $\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$ into the injective resolution $\mathcal J^\bullet$, the map $H^p(\Gamma(S,\gamma)):H^p(\Gamma(S,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet))\to H^p(\Gamma(S,\mathcal J^\bullet))=H^p(S,h_*\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism for every $p\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma 01F4 (lemma-apply-Leray, line 2255) part (1), proved directly as its proof suggests: Remark 01F0 (remark-elucidate-lemma) with Leray's acyclicity lemma, Derived Categories 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity)

proof.text: (This is the edge map.) By [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (c), $e_{h,\mathcal F}=\varphi^*$ for the $h$-map $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$, $\mathcal G=h_*\mathcal F$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (1) $\varphi^*$ does not depend on the choices made in its definition. Make these choices: the injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ of step 2; the injective resolution $s:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ of step 3; as resolution of $h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ by a complex of injectives the quasi-isomorphism $\gamma:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet:=\mathcal J^\bullet$ of step 3; and $\beta=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal J^\bullet}$. The compatibility required of $\beta$ holds: the composite $\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\varphi}h_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\alpha}h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\gamma}\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is $\gamma\circ\alpha=s=\beta\circ s$. The definition then gives $e_{h,\mathcal F}=H^p(\Gamma(S,\gamma))^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(S,\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal J^\bullet}))=H^p(\Gamma(S,\gamma))^{-1}$ as a map $H^p(S,h_*\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(S,\mathcal J^\bullet))\to H^p(\Gamma(S,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. By step 3 it is an isomorphism, and it is $\mathcal O_S(S)$-linear by the definition. Hence $e_{h,\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S(S)$-modules for every $p\ge0$.

lean.statement: theorem affine_morphism_cohomology_edge {X S : Scheme.{v}} (h : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom h] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : (∀ (p : ℕ), 0 < p → IsZero (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage h.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p).obj F)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ), IsIso (moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p) ∧ ∀ (r : Γ(S, ⊤)) (x : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology S.toRingedSpace p).obj ((pushforward h).obj F)), moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p (r • x) = h.appTop r • @id ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F) (moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p x))
lean.note: Positive right-derived module direct images vanish; the recorded identity h-map edge map is invertible and compatible with global-section scalars through h.appTop. No derived-category choices are required.
